chunks: 4089 - And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, who said:

A man wrote to al-Faqīh, peace be upon him, regarding a man who entrusted another man with a deposit and instructed him to place it in his house, or did not instruct him; then the man placed it in his neighbor’s house and it was lost. Is liability binding upon him if he went against his instruction or took it out of his possession?
So he, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: “He is liable for it, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.”

key_terms.جَارِهِ: His neighbor, whose house became the unauthorized place of storage
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: Liable; legally responsible to compensate for the lost property
key_terms.فَضَاعَتْ: It was lost, meaning the entrusted property perished or went missing
key_terms.مَنْزِلِهِ: His house, the designated or expected place of keeping the deposit
key_terms.وَدِيعَةً: A deposited item entrusted to someone for safekeeping
key_terms.يَجِبُ: Becomes binding or obligatory in legal responsibility

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if he moves an entrusted deposit to another place and it is lost?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a deposit (wadīʿah) entrusted for safekeeping. If the trustee moves it from the expected place of custody, especially contrary to instruction, and it is lost, he is held liable for it. The report highlights the legal seriousness of trust and the rights of property owners.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4089 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, who said:

A man wrote to the 'Jurist' (Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as)) regarding a case where someone entrusted another person with a deposit (wadi'ah) and instructed him to keep it in his own house, or gave no specific instruction. However, the man placed it in his neighbor's house, and it was lost.
Does he bear responsibility if he disobeyed the instruction or moved it out of his possession?
The 'Jurist' (Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as)) replied: "He is liable for it, if Allah (swt) wills."
